review.notes:
Chain starts at lineage v4 (SDLI-EN015, 2014-06-27), whose text the baseline's cdb entry matches exactly. Earlier transitions precede the baseline and are behaviourally identical, progressively formalising the same resolution: v0 (LODT-EN022, 2008-05-13, the printing in force at the Edison snapshot) 'You can destroy 1 card on the field'; v1 (GLD4-EN024, 2011-06-24) 'select 1 card on the field, and destroy it'; v2 (SDDC-EN023, 2012-02-03) PSCT 'target 1 card; destroy that target'; v3 (PGLD-EN086, 2014-03-28) adds '(if any), also, after that'; v4 splits into bullets 'Apply these effects in sequence'. EdisonFormat's entry confirms the era behaviour of the v0 printing matches what the v4-era script does, which is why starting the chain at v4 does not misdate the period behaviour. No trailing cosmetic transitions: v5 is the modern text.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Ryko, Lightsworn Hunter). The rulings read support d1 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [event] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d2 unresolved (general rule only) at Edison, unresolved (general rule only) at Tengu.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (YS17-EN017, Starter Deck: Link Strike)

event.historical_text: FLIP: Apply these effects in sequence.● You can target 1 card on the field; destroy that target.● Send the top 3 cards of your Deck to the Graveyard.
event.modern_text: FLIP: Apply these effects (simultaneously).● You can destroy 1 card on the field.● Send the top 3 cards of your Deck to the GY.
event.summary: Functional erratum: the destruction stopped targeting and the two bullets became simultaneous instead of sequential. The pre-errata script sets EFFECT_FLAG_CARD_TARGET and picks the card to destroy inside the FLIP effect's target function (Duel.SelectTarget at activation), then resolves Duel.Destroy -> Duel.BreakEffect() -> Duel.DiscardDeck, so the mill lands at a separate timing after the destruction and other cards can miss timing on it; the modern script has no targeting, chooses the card at resolution and omits BreakEffect, applying destruction and mill simultaneously.

rulings_check.difference: Era: the destruction targets (the card is chosen at activation). Modern (2017): no targeting; the card is chosen at resolution. Era: the destruction and the 3-card mill are applied in sequence, so the mill is a separate timing after the destruction. Modern: applied simultaneously.
